lineage.domain_test: The deciding quantity is the plan's 2027 cost at each annual maximum, the benefit-change pricing a health plan's claims analytics works from a continuance table of its members' annual plan-paid charges; put megawatt-hours or library loans in for dental claims and there is no predetermination, no coinsurance tier and no plan-year reset of a per-person benefit maximum, and the task stops making sense.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what each member's yearly amount would be under a higher per-member ceiling when the records stop at the current one: members who reach it put off work their providers had already priced in advance until the ceiling resets, so that work shows only in the advance estimates and among the next period's first records, and a higher ceiling's cost read from the period's own records misses it and comes out at about half.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each 2025 member's plan-paid amount before the maximum is the 2025 claims (the lines the maximum cut included) plus the predetermined major work the member put off once the estimate showed the 1,500 dollar maximum would cut the payment, read as the 2025 estimate lines whose member, procedure and tooth are not claimed in 2025 and are claimed after 1 January 2026 within the estimate's twelve months; at the 2027 fees that work puts the 3,000 dollar maximum over the board's 1.90 dollars per covered person month and leaves 2,000 dollars inside it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver prices each maximum on a continuance of the 2025 claims re-priced at the 2027 fees and files 3,000 dollars (1.23 per covered person month); members at the 1,500 dollar maximum put off their predetermined crowns, bridges and implants to the January reset, so at a higher maximum the plan pays for that work in the year and only 2,000 dollars (1.55; 3,000 at 2.34) fits the board's 1.90.

lineage.niche: a UK secondary aluminium works' 2026 direct emissions per tonne of each product family (two extrusion billet alloys, foundry ingot, heat-treated castings), conformed from the site gas meter's 15-minute export, the gas supplier's invoices, the melting furnaces' charge logs, the homogenizing furnace and solution oven logs and the production records, for a car maker's 2027 low-carbon premium
lineage.answer: EUR 342,000: Velden pays EUR 38 a tonne on 7,200 t of 6063 extrusion billet and 1,800 t of LM25 foundry ingot, the two families at or under SCR-2's 0.235 t CO2/t in 2026 (6063 billet 0.211, LM25 ingot 0.168); 6082 billet (0.263) and the LM25-TF castings (0.501) are over the limit

world.geography: United Kingdom, West Midlands (a fictional secondary aluminium works with a casthouse and a sand foundry, and a fictional German car maker; the companies and people are fictional)
world.org_type: a secondary aluminium works supplying a car maker under its supplier carbon requirement

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is each product's share of fuel burned by shared equipment, recorded only by one meter, where one process burns fuel by the mass it melts and others by the hours they hold heat whatever they hold; spreading the meter's fuel over the products by their output mass gives every product the plant's average, while the processes' own fuel, read from the meter's response to when each process runs and how much it melts, puts the long-soaked product and the low-yield product well above it.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each family's 2026 direct emissions are the gas its processes burned: melting attributed by the tonnes melted for the family (castings melt about 1.6 tonnes per tonne shipped), the homogenizing furnace by its firing hours on the family's loads (6082 billet soaks about twice as long as 6063), the solution oven only to the castings, and the gas burned with no process running shared by tonnes; each process's gas is read from the site meter's 15-minute record against the charge and furnace logs, since no process is sub-metered.
lineage.stump: The default path reads each process's gas from the site meter as a quantity per tonne and gives the homogenizing furnace's gas to the two billet alloys by the tonnes each put through it, so 6082 billet sits level with 6063 at 0.225 t CO2/t and the premium comes to EUR 456,000; the furnace burns by the hour whatever a load weighs, a 6082 load soaks about 15 hours against about 6 for 6063, and 6082 takes 47 per cent of the furnace's hours on 26 per cent of its billet, which puts it at 0.263, over the limit, and the premium at EUR 342,000.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-07 on its first portal round: both responses landed the golden premium of EUR 342,000, allocating the homogenizing furnace's gas by its loads' firing hours, the method a careful analyst reaches for, which the hourly gas fitted at R-squared 0.9985; Domains Fit flagged; the emissions-inventory world and the furnace-allocation driver are spent
